title: Case-row locks and outbox stream inserts never deadlock, and a deadlocked batch upload request is retried
source: docs/evidence/step-9/s9-2/result-g.json databaseDeadlocks: 11 reports, every cycle names INSERT INTO usp_outbox_streams and SELECT id,revision,archived,frame,context,site_id FROM cases WHERE id=$1 FOR UPDATE
whyTheInsertWaits: The stream id is case-ingestion:<caseId>:<access> (events.ts:28): one row per case and access context; it does not change with the case context, frame or site.

appendUspOutboxTx (outbox.ts:5) inserts the stream row ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then updates its last_sequence. The unique check of a later insert finds the row version another open transaction wrote (its uncommitted new row or its uncommitted last_sequence update) and waits for that transaction to end.
So every append holds the case stream until commit, like an exclusive lock taken after the case row lock.

change.lockOrder: document-worker.ts failDocumentJob: a stale end first locks its case with SELECT c.id FROM cases c JOIN jobs j ON j.case_id=c.id WHERE j.id=$1 FOR UPDATE OF c, before the job row and any stream append; FOR UPDATE is the strongest mode the re-queue takes. This also matches the claim and acceptance order (case, then job). Other ends (failed, not stale) take no case lock, as before.
change.otherCallSites: Every other caller of documentCaseTx/documentSourceTx/assertDocumentInputTx with lock=true takes it as its first case statement (receipt, retry, claim, acceptance beforeLocks, layout reservation, association, claims, proposals); the intake publish path locks FOR UPDATE before queueBatchDocumentTx. Unchanged.
change.kept: no lock weakened or removed, no schema change, outbox sequence and event bodies unchanged

retry.helper: deadlock-retry.ts retryRolledBack: reruns the whole transaction on 40P01 or 40001, at most 2 more times, after a 20 to 99 ms random delay; any other error and the third rollback are thrown unchanged

routes.safe: rows, request key (usp_source_uploads.request_key), quota reservation and upload.changed event are all inside it; the storage profile check runs before it and is not repeated; no object is written; new ids are drawn again only because the first ones rolled back

routes.wrapped: claim, pre-storage fence and publication transactions
routes.safe: each is DB only; the original is written between them under the fixed key large-originals/<sourceId>/<sha256>, never inside a retried callback; the lease token of a rolled-back claim was never stored; failure() and cleanup are not retried
item row, operations request key, jobs and every outbox event are inside each; the probe reads the original once between them and its result is reused; no object is written on this path
